title: Joseph and Pharaoh's Dream
summary: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows and seven thin cows, and no one in Egypt can understand the dream. Joseph explains that seven years of plenty will come, followed by seven years of hunger, and suggests storing food in big storehouses. A story about wisdom, planning ahead and caring for everyone.
pages:
In a great palace in Egypt, King Pharaoh was sleeping.
He slept in a soft bed, with golden pillows.
But his sleep was not peaceful.

Pharaoh dreamed he was standing by the Nile.
Out of the water came seven fat, beautiful cows, "Moooo!"
And they ate green grass.

After them came seven other cows – very, very thin.
And the thin cows ate up the fat cows,
but stayed just as thin as before!

Pharaoh woke up with a fright.
He went back to sleep and dreamed again:
seven full ears of grain, and seven thin ears of grain that swallowed them up.

In the morning Pharaoh called all the wise men of Egypt.
"What does the dream mean?" he asked.
The wise men scratched their heads and shrugged their shoulders. Nobody knew.

Then the chief cupbearer remembered:
"In the prison there is a Hebrew young man, Joseph.
He explains dreams!"
And right away they brought Joseph to the palace.

"I have heard that you know how to explain dreams," said Pharaoh.
"Not I," answered Joseph, "God is the One who knows.
But tell me, and I will try to help."

Pharaoh told him, and Joseph listened carefully.
"The two dreams are really one dream," he said.
"The seven fat cows are seven good years, with lots and lots of food."

"And the seven thin cows are seven hard years of hunger.
In them almost nothing will grow.
But I have an idea!"

"In the good years we will build big storehouses,
and keep some of the wheat in them.
And when the hunger comes – everyone will have something to eat."

"What a wise idea!" cried Pharaoh.
He gave Joseph a ring, a gold chain and white clothes.
"You will be in charge of all of Egypt!"

And sure enough, seven good years came, and Joseph gathered and stored, gathered and stored.
And when the hard years came – the storehouses were full,
and people from every land came to buy food.

Joseph thought ahead, and took care of everyone.
You can think ahead too:
pack your bag the night before, save a treat for tomorrow, or set aside a piece for a friend.
